name: Mickey Gall
event: UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Nolan
summary: Jiu-jitsu-first veteran (7-7; 6-7 UFC), 34-35, on a four-fight losing streak with no win since July 2021 and no fight since a R1 knockout loss to Ramiz Brahimaj in November 2024. Was pulled from a September return for failing medicals; now cleared and moving up to middleweight against Zach Reese.

how_they_fight.Striking: Upright and hittable: absorbs about 5.5 significant strikes a minute and lands about 4.3. Will throw a jab-right (stung Brahimaj with one per Cageside Press) but loses most kickboxing exchanges with real strikers.
how_they_fight.Grappling: All six of his stoppage wins are submissions (five in R1, Northcutt in R2), mostly rear-naked chokes off scrambles or a back-take. Takedown entries are weak (about 36%), so he needs opponents to grapple with him or give up a position.
how_they_fight.Defense: Stopped three times, all by strikes: Diego Sanchez (R2, after being taken down and controlled), Mike Malott (R1), Brahimaj (R1). Never submitted. Takedown defense about 45%.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Early or not at all: every finish win came by R2 (five R1). Once past R1 he's 1-4 in decisions (beat Touahri; lost to Brown, Perry, Morono, Hafez). His KO losses came R1 (2) and R2 (1). Not a late-rounds fighter.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Reads submission chances quickly, but has tended to stand and trade when takedowns aren't there.

patterns: Back-takes and rear-naked chokes in R1
Loses decisions when he can't get the fight down
Knocked out in R1 in two of his last three
concerns: Nearly two years out, a medical flag in September, and a first fight at middleweight
Chin and defense: three KO losses, two in R1
keys_to_beat: Stay on the feet and throw at volume; he gets hit a lot
Don't give up the back in scrambles; stay heavy on top or stand
Pressure early - he has not looked better as fights go on

news.text: Pulled from his UFC Vegas 121 return against Sedriques Dumas after pre-fight medicals flagged an undisclosed issue; Gall called the fix a simple procedure.
Cageside Press said the Dumas bout would have been his first at middleweight; Boxing News listed it at welterweight.
Cleared and booked against Zach Reese at middleweight for Oct 31 (MMA Junkie, two sources).
